metadata.title: Combined stimuli: philosophical families + modality contrast set

philosophical.title: Philosophical Contradictions and Paradoxes: Seed Questions
philosophical.purpose: Seed stimuli for examining how a language model represents contradictions, paradoxes, and related conceptual puzzles.
philosophical.response_instruction: Classify the statement using exactly one label: coherent, contradiction, paradox, or underdetermined. Then explain the classification in one sentence.

labels.coherent: The statement describes a logically and conceptually consistent situation.
labels.contradiction: The statement jointly asserts conditions that cannot all be true in the stated respect and context.
labels.paradox: The statement or construction generates an apparent contradiction through self-reference, circularity, infinity, or a rule system.
labels.underdetermined: The statement raises a genuine conceptual question but does not itself entail a contradiction.

notes: These are seed examples, not a statistically balanced evaluation set.
Paradoxes are kept separate from direct contradictions.
Each item includes a nearby coherent control and several surface-form transformations.
For activation experiments, use the full prompt and record the hidden state immediately before the model generates its classification.

modality.title: Modality Contrast Set: True, False, Improbable, Anomalous, Impossible
modality.purpose: Topic-matched families separating necessary falsehood (impossibility) from contingent falsehood, improbability, and semantic anomaly.
modality.design: Each family shares one topic and contains five declarative statements: a common truth, a contingent falsehood, an improbable-but-possible claim, a semantically anomalous sentence, and a necessarily false (impossible) statement. Impossibility constructions are varied (reflexive comparison, temporal reversal, part-whole counting, definitional violation, kinship circularity, explicit conjunction) to avoid a single lexical template.
modality.modality_encoding: The modality of each item is encoded in its id suffix: _true, _false, _improbable, _anomalous, _impossible. The family is the id's middle token.
modality.response_instruction: Classify the statement using exactly one label: coherent, contradiction, paradox, or underdetermined. Then explain the classification in one sentence.

prompt_template:
Statement: {statement}

Classify the statement using exactly one label: coherent, contradiction, paradox, or underdetermined. Then explain the classification in one sentence.

items.name: Direct contradiction
items.statement_en: The same proposition is both true and false at the same time and in the same respect.
items.statement_ko: 동일한 명제가 같은 시간, 같은 관점에서 참이면서 동시에 거짓이다.
transformations: Proposition P is true, and proposition P is not true, in precisely the same sense.
It is the case that P and not-P.
Can one proposition be both true and not true simultaneously in the very same respect?
items.coherent_control: One proposition is true while a different proposition is false at the same time.

items.name: Red and not red
items.statement_en: The object is entirely red and not red at the same time, in the same place, and in the same respect.
items.statement_ko: 그 물체는 같은 시간과 장소, 같은 관점에서 완전히 빨갛고 동시에 빨갛지 않다.
transformations: In the same respect, the object is wholly red while also being non-red.
This object has and does not have the property of redness under identical conditions.
Is an object consistently describable as red and not red in exactly the same respect?
items.coherent_control: The object is red on one side and not red on the other side.

items.name: Married bachelor
items.statement_en: There exists a married bachelor.
transformations: A man is both married and a bachelor in the ordinary senses of those words.
Someone who has a spouse is an unmarried man.
Could a person be a married bachelor without changing either definition?
items.coherent_control: There exists a formerly married bachelor.

items.name: Square circle
items.statement_en: A plane figure is both a perfect square and a perfect circle in the same geometric respect.
items.statement_ko: 하나의 평면 도형이 같은 기하학적 관점에서 완전한 정사각형이면서 완전한 원이다.
transformations: There is a Euclidean square circle.
One ordinary plane figure has exactly four straight sides and a boundary whose points are all equally distant from its center.
Can an ordinary Euclidean figure be simultaneously a square and a circle?
items.coherent_control: A square is drawn inside a circle.

items.name: Three-sided square
items.statement_en: This Euclidean square has exactly three sides.
items.statement_ko: 이 유클리드 정사각형은 정확히 세 변을 가진다.
transformations: A three-sided figure is an ordinary square.
The polygon has four sides by definition, yet it has only three sides.
Can a Euclidean square have exactly three edges?
items.coherent_control: This Euclidean square has exactly four sides.

items.name: Largest integer
items.statement_en: There is a largest integer, and adding one to it does not produce a larger integer.
items.statement_ko: 가장 큰 정수가 존재하며, 거기에 1을 더해도 더 큰 정수가 되지 않는다.
transformations: Some integer N is greater than or equal to every integer, including N plus one.
The integers end at a final greatest member.
Can the ordinary integers contain a greatest integer?
items.coherent_control: A finite set of integers has a largest member.

items.name: Liar paradox
items.statement_en: This sentence is false.
transformations: The sentence you are now reading is not true.
This very assertion asserts its own falsity.
Is the statement 'This statement is false' true or false?

items.name: Strengthened liar paradox
items.statement_en: This sentence is not true.
transformations: The present statement fails to be true.
This very utterance has no truth.
Can the sentence 'This sentence is not true' consistently be assigned a truth value?
items.coherent_control: The sentence 'Snow is black' is not true under ordinary conditions.

items.name: Epimenides-style liar
items.statement_en: A Cretan says, 'Every statement made by a Cretan is false.'
items.statement_ko: 한 크레타인이 '모든 크레타인의 발언은 거짓이다'라고 말한다.
transformations: Someone from Crete declares that no Cretan ever speaks truly.
A member of a group claims that every claim by members of that group is false.
Does a Cretan saying 'All Cretans always lie' create a strict contradiction by itself?
items.coherent_control: A Cretan says, 'Some statements made by Cretans are false.'

items.name: Russell's paradox
items.statement_en: Let R be the set of all sets that are not members of themselves. R is a member of itself if and only if R is not a member of itself.
items.statement_ko: 자기 자신을 원소로 포함하지 않는 모든 집합의 집합을 R이라 하자. R은 자기 자신의 원소일 때 그리고 오직 그때에만 자기 자신의 원소가 아니다.
transformations: The set of every non-self-membered set belongs to itself exactly when it does not belong to itself.
Define R = {x | x is not an element of x}; asking whether R is an element of R yields both alternatives.
Does the unrestricted set of all sets that do not contain themselves contain itself?
items.coherent_control: Let R be the set of all finite sets that are not members of themselves.

items.name: Barber paradox
items.statement_en: A barber shaves all and only those villagers who do not shave themselves.
items.statement_ko: 한 이발사는 스스로 면도하지 않는 마을 사람들만, 그리고 그들 모두를 면도한다.
transformations: The barber shaves exactly every person in the village who does not shave themself.
For every villager x, the barber shaves x if and only if x does not shave x.
Under this rule, can the barber consistently either shave or not shave himself?
items.coherent_control: A barber shaves every villager who requests a shave but does not shave himself.

items.name: Omnipotence paradox
items.statement_en: An omnipotent being creates a stone that the being cannot lift.
items.statement_ko: 전능한 존재가 자신이 들 수 없는 돌을 만든다.
transformations: A being capable of every action makes an object that defeats its own power.
An all-powerful agent performs the task of making something it is powerless to move.
Can an omnipotent being make a stone too heavy for that same being to lift?
items.coherent_control: A very powerful but limited being creates a stone that it cannot lift.

items.name: Irresistible force and immovable object
items.statement_en: An irresistible force strikes an absolutely immovable object.
items.statement_ko: 멈출 수 없는 힘이 절대로 움직일 수 없는 물체와 충돌한다.
transformations: A force that nothing can stop meets an object that nothing can move.
The perfectly unstoppable encounters the perfectly unmovable.
What happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable object?
items.coherent_control: A very strong force strikes an object that is extremely difficult to move.

items.name: Grandfather paradox
items.statement_en: A time traveler goes into the past and prevents their own grandfather from having children, while the traveler still exists as that grandchild.
items.statement_ko: 시간 여행자가 과거로 가서 자신의 할아버지가 자녀를 갖지 못하게 하지만, 그 시간 여행자는 여전히 그 손주로 존재한다.
transformations: A traveler erases a necessary cause of their own birth without erasing themself.
Someone exists because of an event and then travels backward to prevent that event while continuing to exist.
Can a person prevent their own ancestry and nevertheless remain the descendant produced by it?
items.coherent_control: A time traveler goes into the past and unsuccessfully attempts to prevent their grandfather from having children.

items.name: Sorites paradox
items.statement_en: One grain of sand is not a heap, and adding a single grain can never turn a non-heap into a heap; therefore, no number of grains forms a heap.
items.statement_ko: 모래 한 알은 더미가 아니며 한 알을 더하는 것으로 더미 아닌 것이 더미가 될 수는 없으므로, 어떤 수의 모래알도 더미를 이루지 못한다.
transformations: If one grain is not a heap and one extra grain never makes the decisive difference, then even a million grains are not a heap.
Repeatedly applying the harmless-looking one-grain step eliminates every possible heap.
If adding one grain never creates a heap, how can any heap exist?
items.coherent_control: One grain is not ordinarily called a heap, while a million grains often are.

items.name: Ship of Theseus
items.statement_en: Every plank of a ship is gradually replaced, and the resulting ship is claimed to be numerically identical to the original ship.
items.statement_ko: 배의 모든 널빤지를 점차 교체한 뒤, 그렇게 생긴 배가 원래 배와 수적으로 동일한 배라고 주장한다.
transformations: After all of an object's components are replaced one by one, it remains the very same object.
The completely rebuilt ship is identical, not merely similar, to the original.
Does replacing every component of a ship cause it to cease being the same ship?
items.coherent_control: Every plank of a ship is repainted, and the ship remains the same ship.

items.name: Colorless green ideas
items.statement_en: Colorless green ideas sleep furiously.
transformations: Furiously sleeping ideas are both green and colorless.
Ideas without color possess greenness and engage in furious sleep.
Is the grammatical sentence 'Colorless green ideas sleep furiously' semantically coherent?

items.name: Paris — true
items.statement_en: Paris is the capital of France.

items.name: Paris — false
items.statement_en: Paris is the capital of Germany.

items.name: Paris — improbable
items.statement_en: Every train into Paris arrived exactly on time for an entire month.

items.name: Paris — anomalous
items.statement_en: Paris quietly drinks its own gray arithmetic every evening.

items.name: Paris — impossible
items.statement_en: Paris is larger than itself.

items.name: Boiling water — true
items.statement_en: At sea level, water boils at about one hundred degrees Celsius.

items.name: Boiling water — false
items.statement_en: At sea level, water boils at about fifty degrees Celsius.

items.name: Boiling water — improbable
items.statement_en: One determined cook boiled the same kettle four hundred times in a single day.

items.name: Boiling water — anomalous
items.statement_en: The boiling water argued with its own steam about the ethics of temperature.

items.name: Boiling water — impossible
items.statement_en: The water in this kettle froze solid while remaining entirely liquid.

items.name: Heart — true
items.statement_en: The human heart pumps blood through the body.

items.name: Heart — false
items.statement_en: The human heart is located inside the skull.

items.name: Heart — improbable
items.statement_en: A patient's resting heart rate stayed at exactly sixty beats per minute for a full day.

items.name: Heart — anomalous
items.statement_en: The heart files its red paperwork under a language of thumps.

items.name: Heart — impossible
items.statement_en: The heart completed its final beat before its first beat.

items.name: Everest — true
items.statement_en: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.

items.name: Everest — false
items.statement_en: Mount Everest is located in the Alps.

items.name: Everest — improbable
items.statement_en: An eighty-year-old climber reached the summit of Everest twice in one season.

items.name: Everest — anomalous
items.statement_en: Everest rehearses its patient snow in green syllables.

items.name: Everest — impossible
items.statement_en: Mount Everest is taller than Mount Everest.

items.name: Whale — true
items.statement_en: Whales are mammals that breathe air.

items.name: Whale — false
items.statement_en: Whales are fish that breathe through gills.

items.name: Whale — improbable
items.statement_en: A lone whale followed the same cargo ship for ten consecutive years.

items.name: Whale — anomalous
items.statement_en: The whale swallowed a polite argument and swam through its own name.

items.name: Whale — impossible
items.statement_en: This whale is the biological mother of her own mother.

items.name: Rain — true
items.statement_en: Rain falls from clouds in the sky.

items.name: Rain — false
items.statement_en: Rain is composed mostly of salt water.

items.name: Rain — improbable
items.statement_en: Rain fell on this town every single day for two full years.

items.name: Rain — anomalous
items.statement_en: The rain divided its gray ideas among the impatient umbrellas.

items.name: Rain — impossible
items.statement_en: More rain fell this morning than fell during the whole day that contains this morning.

items.name: Apples — true
items.statement_en: Apples grow on trees.

items.name: Apples — false
items.statement_en: Apples grow underground like potatoes.

items.name: Apples — improbable
items.statement_en: Every apple in the orchard fell to the ground during the same minute.

items.name: Apples — anomalous
items.statement_en: The apples counted their green silence backwards into ripeness.

items.name: Apples — impossible
items.statement_en: The basket holds more apples than it holds pieces of fruit.

items.name: Bachelor — true
items.statement_en: Some bachelors eventually marry.

items.name: Bachelor — false
items.statement_en: Most bachelors in the world are over ninety years old.

items.name: Bachelor — improbable
items.statement_en: Every bachelor in the village got married on the same afternoon.

items.name: Bachelor — anomalous
items.statement_en: A bachelor of pale arithmetic proposed to the idea of Tuesday.

items.name: Bachelor — impossible
items.statement_en: A married bachelor lives in the village.

items.name: Triangle — true
items.statement_en: A triangle has exactly three sides.

items.name: Triangle — false
items.statement_en: Triangles were first described by mathematicians only in the nineteenth century.

items.name: Triangle — improbable
items.statement_en: A student drew ten thousand triangles by hand in one afternoon.

items.name: Triangle — anomalous
items.statement_en: The triangle sleeps soundly inside its own colorless angles.

items.name: Triangle — impossible
items.statement_en: This Euclidean triangle has exactly four sides.

items.name: Grandmother — true
items.statement_en: Many grandmothers help raise their grandchildren.

items.name: Grandmother — false
items.statement_en: Most grandmothers today are under thirty years old.

items.name: Grandmother — improbable
items.statement_en: One woman became a great-grandmother at the age of fifty.

items.name: Grandmother — anomalous
items.statement_en: Grandmother knitted a sweater out of warm green silence.

items.name: Grandmother — impossible
items.statement_en: She is her own biological grandmother.

items.name: Sun — true
items.statement_en: The sun rises in the east.

items.name: Sun — false
items.statement_en: The sun is smaller than the Earth.

items.name: Sun — improbable
items.statement_en: The coastal town saw five hundred consecutive days without a single cloud.

items.name: Sun — anomalous
items.statement_en: The sun whispers its yellow logic to a sleeping number.

items.name: Sun — impossible
items.statement_en: Tomorrow's sunrise took place yesterday.

items.name: Library — true
items.statement_en: Public libraries lend books to readers.

items.name: Library — false
items.statement_en: Most public libraries were abolished worldwide in the nineteen nineties.

items.name: Library — improbable
items.statement_en: One reader borrowed and finished a library book every day for forty years.

items.name: Library — anomalous
items.statement_en: The library shelves its dusty Tuesdays in alphabetical order.

items.name: Library — impossible
items.statement_en: This library contains more books than the total number of books in existence.

items.name: Gold — true
items.statement_en: Gold is a metal that does not rust.

items.name: Gold — false
items.statement_en: Gold rusts within days when exposed to dry air.

items.name: Gold — improbable
items.statement_en: A hiker found gold nuggets on three separate walks in a single week.

items.name: Gold — anomalous
items.statement_en: The gold counts its heavy yellow dreams every night.

items.name: Gold — impossible
items.statement_en: This ring is made entirely of gold and contains no gold at all.

items.name: Penguin — true
items.statement_en: Penguins are birds that cannot fly.

items.name: Penguin — false
items.statement_en: Penguins live wild at the North Pole.

items.name: Penguin — improbable
items.statement_en: A penguin wandered one hundred kilometers inland and returned to the colony unharmed.

items.name: Penguin — anomalous
items.statement_en: The penguin recites its colorless ice to a distant equator.

items.name: Penguin — impossible
items.statement_en: This penguin is a bird and is not a bird, in the very same sense.

items.name: Train — true
items.statement_en: Trains run on rails.

items.name: Train — false
items.statement_en: Most modern passenger trains are pulled by teams of horses.

items.name: Train — improbable
items.statement_en: The night train arrived early every single day for an entire year.

items.name: Train — anomalous
items.statement_en: The train devours a timetable of green minutes.

items.name: Train — impossible
items.statement_en: On the same trip, the train arrived at its destination before it departed.
